newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn accused of pushing 1996 deficit over targets.
newsitem.headline: Bonn accused of pushing 1996 deficit over targets.

text.p: A budget expert from Germany's opposition SPD party on Monday accused the government of pushing the country's budget deficit to record highs and far above agreed targets for 1996.

The SPD's Karl Diller said in a statement that Germany's budget deficit was 92.8 billion marks at the end of November, some 33 billion marks more than the 59.9 billion marks approved by parliament in the budget for 1996.

Diller acknowledged that the year-end figure would be lower because of numerous tax payments due in December, but said finance minister Theo Waigel and chancellor Helmut Kohl would still be remembered as Germany's greatest ever debt-creators.
Diller said the disparity between spending and income was due to inadequate returns from privatisations and a fall-off in taxation returns.
The government has said in the past that Germany's budget deficit would total some 73 billion marks this year.
